page.notes: Verse set in italic lines; each line is printed as one line, rendered here with line breaks inside a paragraph. The marginal note "Anacreon" stands at the right beside the line "Orpheus: quam facili pollice" (the printed mark ⸻ in the margin). The word "Et" at the bottom right is a catchword/signature-like fragment set in the right margin, in roman type. The Greek-letter-free text is all Latin. Doubtful: "Beζam" is a misreading of the printed name, which appears to be "Bezam" with a long-s-like form; "asl" likely "ast" (= at); "Mulcent Ausonijs" likely "Ausonijs" printed as "Ausonijs". Marginal mark "Ζ" is not reliable; "Be[?]am" should be read as the printed name. Some accents over vowels in "Æolium", "Cithara" are printed macron/tilde variants.
